name: Yixing zisha teapot
summary: Small unglazed teapots in the red-brown stoneware of Yixing. The potter builds them by hand, and the porous wall takes a patina from the tea that it holds.

philosophy.core_thesis: A teapot for steeped tea needs no glaze: a dense, porous clay keeps the tea hot and the taste pure, and the pot improves with use.
design_principles: Leave the clay bare, so that the wall can take up the oil and the colour of the tea.
Build the wall by hand from slabs and strips, 2 to 4 mm thick.
Make the lid fit the body so well that a closed spout makes the lid hold when the pot is turned over.
Make one pot hold 100 to 300 ml, for one drinker or a small group.
Choose one form for one clay: a round pot for smooth clay, a square pot for coarse clay.
Cut calligraphy or a poem into the wall, and stamp the maker's seal under the lid and on the base.
Fire the pot at 1100 to 1200 °C so that the body is dense but still takes water.
Use one clay for one kind of tea, and do not wash it with soap.
anti_patterns: A thick glossy glaze that closes the pores of the wall
A pot of mixed clays that is fired many times for effect
A heavy, thick wall of 8 mm or more
A hand-painted flower pattern in bright enamel colours

form.shape: A small teapot with a short spout, a strap handle or a side handle, and a lid with a knob. Forms follow nature or geometry: pumpkin, bamboo, lotus, a plain sphere or a square.
form.profile: A round or faceted body on a flat base. The spout rises from the shoulder to the height of the rim, and the lid sits flush with the mouth.
form.foot_and_rim: A flat, bare base with a small ring or three short feet; a flange inside the mouth holds the lid and the rim is cut square.
form.proportion: Height 6 to 12 cm and capacity 100 to 300 ml. The spout, the handle and the knob lie on one axis, and the wall is 2 to 4 mm thick.
rules: Keep the pot small and the wall thin.
Align the spout mouth, the rim and the handle top on one level line.
Fit the lid so tightly that it needs no glaze to seal.
Stamp the seal of the maker inside the lid and under the base.

bodies.rule: Use zisha, an iron-rich clay from the hills of Yixing. Fire it to a dense, unglazed body. Keep porcelain and glazed bodies out of the pot.

methods: pounding the clay into flat slabs and strips
wrapping a slab round a wooden form to make the body
adding the spout, handle and lid as separate parts
smoothing the wall with a steel scraper and a bamboo knife
polishing with a smooth bone or a damp cloth
forming.joins: The spout and the handle are luted with slip on a cut and scored seat; the lid is cut from the body and ground to fit.
forming.details: Seams are hidden, the lid is ground to a perfect fit, and the maker stamps a seal on the base and under the lid.

glaze.pattern: Bare clay in purple-brown, red or buff; an incised poem or a bamboo branch, or a sprigged plum blossom on the wall.
glaze.gloss: Matt to soft satin, about 2 to 25 GU; hand and tea polish the surface over the years.
glaze.wear: The wall darkens and shines where hands hold it and where tea touches it. Tea oil fills the pores.

palette.strategy: Earth tones from one clay: purple-brown, red-brown, buff and a rare dark green. Each pot keeps one tone.

firing.kiln: A dragon kiln on a hill slope for the pots in saggars, and later a small bottle kiln; fired with wood.
processes: stacking each pot with its lid in a saggar
slow cooling in the closed kiln
firing.scale: A craft of small workshops in the town of Yixing; a master made one pot in several days, and the best pots are single pieces.
firing.signs: Small colour changes where the flame touched the clay, a seal on the base, and fine lines where the slabs were joined.

emotion.target_response: A slow, private calm. The viewer sees a small plain pot that a hand has worn smooth and thinks of one quiet cup of tea.

modifiers.how: Cover the body with a clear crackle glaze and paint it in overglaze enamel and gold.

modifiers.request: European, with a spout and a gilt rim
modifiers.how: Change the body to soft-paste porcelain with a glaze and add enamel flowers and gilding.

wall_thickness.note: Zisha walls are thin; the wall stays under 5 mm.
